newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 1.50 cents lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 1.50 cents lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.50 cents lower Wednesday as dealers expect the market to pull back following Tuesday's strong finish.

New York arabica futures ended broadly higher on Tuesday, helped by a bullish USDA attache report for the 1997/98 Brazil crop. September arabicas settled up 5.95 cents at 171.65 cents a lb after ranging from 173.00 to 165.00. Spot July ended 6.25 cents higher at 191.50 cents, while the outer months closed up 2.25 to 3.75 cents.

The attache report, dated May 9, put Brazil's 1997/98 harvest at 24 million 60-kg bags, down sharply from the USDA's official Brazil estimate of 28 million bags published in its 1997/98 world coffee production report in June.

USDA stated in the report that the "supply-and-demand projections made by the attache in this report do not represent the USDA's official estimates, but are one source of information used in compiling those official estimates."

Technically, traders said September faced near-term resistance at 174.00-175.00 cents, followed by 181.00 and 184.50. On the downside, Tuesday's low of 165.00 should supply good support, they said, with roaster interest noted in the low 160s.
Weather Services Corp said on Wednesday that there was no damaging cold weather in sight for Brazil's coffee belt, with temperatures expected to be near to above normal during the next seven days.
After Tuesday's close, CSCE reported stocks rose by 2,893 60-kg bags as of July 7, to 55,369 bags. An additional 34,159 bags were pending exchange approval, CSCE said.
London robusta futures were up at midday on Wednesday, but off highs as origin sales pared gains. At the break, benchmark September stood $27 higher at $1,812, after peaking at $1,835.
